newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish pension funding bill nears debate - finmin.
newsitem.headline: Polish pension funding bill nears debate - finmin.

text.p: The Polish government is likely to discuss a crucial bill on funding the proposed pension system reform from privatisation revenues within the next several weeks, Finance Minister Marek Belka said on Wednesday.
"I think the draft law should be discussed by the government within several weeks and passed on to parliament," Belka told reporters before a meeting of the cabinet's economic ministers.
Under the current proposal, the government would issue convertible bonds exchangeable for shares of privatised firms to finance social security reform.
The bonds would be exchangeable for shares in a group of up to 100 companies.
Funds raised by the bond issues would be injected to the state-owned Social Security Office (ZUS), which under the reform plan would lose part of the premiums it now gets.
This part of the premium taken away from ZUS would go to the planned privately-managed pension funds, which would invest in safe securities under close government supervision.

Government officials have said that the bonds could be issued in 1999 or even next year if parliament passed several crucial bills triggering the reform, including the one mentioned by the finance minister, in 1997.
But many politicians and analysts say party bickering before this year's parliamentary elections due around mid-September is likely to delay passage of the reform plan well beyond this year.
